strategic_horizon.terminal_goal: Build a personal weak-network VPN for OpenWrt/Linux to Linux or Windows using unordered FakeTCP/FEC carriers plus a native standards-compliant DTLS 1.3 WBD security/session layer. Xray/VLESS/Vision/REALITY, WireGuard and Android are not part of the V2.1 product stack.
strategic_horizon.current_milestone: V2-M1 reproduce pinned one-lane udp2raw + UDPspeeder product baseline; V2-M2 is native DTLS 1.3 security
strategic_horizon.local_optimization_stop_rule: Finish exact local V2-M1 raw/FEC reproduction before implementing DTLS. Do not write a new FEC protocol, add two lanes, start kernel-anchor work, implement native TUN/session features or Auto until M1 passes. After M1, V2-M2 must use real DTLS 1.3 with certificate/hostname verification; do not add Xray/WireGuard back and do not implement a custom TLS-looking post-handshake cipher or detector-specific fingerprint shaping.

continuation_cursor.last_completed_action: Revised the active V2 architecture to V2.1 at substantive checkpoint fc73c3bb0079e0d1458845d922eeaa4579c74c1b. The carrier decision remains pinned udp2raw-compatible FakeTCP + UDPspeeder FEC, but Xray/VLESS/Vision/REALITY and WireGuard are removed. ADR-0003 now makes WBD itself the security/session owner using standards-compliant DTLS 1.3. FEC is placed before DTLS application-record encryption: each UDPspeeder source/repair datagram becomes an independently authenticated DTLS application datagram, then crosses udp2raw FakeTCP. Initial DTLS implementation pin is wolfSSL v5.9.2-stable / ac01707f552c611fbd135cc723b2682b3e7f80f2 and is architecture-pinned but not locally qualified. A future two-lane mode uses two independent DTLS associations and one merged FEC decoder. ADR-0002 kernel-anchor/real-return-packet research remains independent. Intervening commits 8c4dd105acb47973327d28e43143636b1b93d3d0 and 87aca2bdc39d9921bcd9689df1c42af85ca6daa1 were reconciled as temporary V2-M1 Actions relay helpers for pinned baseline binaries and iptables tooling; they are preserved but do not constitute local runtime qualification. Repository handoff/continuity and Go tests pass at the substantive V2.1 checkpoint; local V2-M1 runtime qualification is still pending.
continuation_cursor.current_task: V2-M1: locally reproduce the exact pinned one-lane udp2raw + UDPspeeder transport as the V2 product baseline. Do not start DTLS implementation until this raw/FEC baseline is locally measured and recorded.
continuation_cursor.why_now: M10-004 already proved the unordered udp2raw + UDPspeeder reference has the weak-network latency class V2 wants. V2.1 changes only the later security/product composition. Keeping M1 unchanged preserves a clean baseline so V2-M2 can measure the incremental cost and behavior of real DTLS 1.3 instead of confounding carrier and security changes.
continuation_cursor.done_when: The local sandbox/privileged host restores or rebuilds the exact udp2raw e5ecd33ec4c25d499a14213a5d1dbd5d21e0dd63 and UDPspeeder 61b24a369700c3d8248dd18fa9a524b778741454 versions, verifies source/archive/binary SHA-256 identities, runs the one-lane UDP -> UDPspeeder -> udp2raw FakeTCP -> udp2raw -> UDPspeeder -> UDP echo topology at approximately 50 ms RTT over 0/1/5/10/15% impairment with both 20:10 and 20:20 where practical, records machine-readable p50/p95/p99/delivery/bytes/CPU results, and confirms the result class matches the qualified M10-004 reference. Remove temporary relay workflows after they have served this task. GitHub Actions may relay bytes but cannot substitute for local execution.
continuation_cursor.next_atomic_action: V2-M1: reconcile the temporary relay helpers at 8c4dd105... and 87aca2bd..., obtain/verify the exact pinned udp2raw and UDPspeeder assets, then execute the simplest one-lane local UDP -> UDPspeeder -> udp2raw FakeTCP -> udp2raw -> UDPspeeder -> UDP echo baseline and the 0/1/5/10/15% impairment sweep. Record local qualification and clean up temporary relay workflows. Only after M1 passes, advance to V2-M2 from ADR-0003: wolfSSL DTLS 1.3 shim between UDPspeeder and udp2raw with a real X.509 certificate and strict peer/hostname verification.
